text:
IncidentBot: Paging: elevated 5xx observed from api-gateway -> multiple customers affected. Trigger: 5xx rate > 3% for 5m :pager:
maya: seeing a big spike in 503s from gateway-01 -> envoy upstream shows 503, timeouts. cc @sam @liam
sam: noticed retries spiking on the LB. dashboard: request_retries_count up 10x in the last 10m.
liam: starting quick check: `kubectl get pods -n gateway -l app=envoy -o wide` -> all pods healthy, CPU nominal.
nisha: logs from gateway-01: `upstream reset before response` and `stream reset by remote` repeated. Paste of logs: ```[2026-03-15T14:20:12Z] proxy error: upstream reset, code:503, route: /v1/generate```
maya: can someone grab envoy /stats on gateway-01/admin? `curl http://gateway-01:9901/stats | grep retries`
sam: output snippet: ```cluster.backend_cluster.upstream_rq_retry: 8243
cluster.backend_cluster.upstream_rq_retry_overflow: 0```
liam: retries are high. Do we have a retry-on-5xx policy at the route level? I remember we added a route-level retry to hide transient errors.
nisha: yes, route config has `retry_policy: retry_on: 5xx, num_retries: 3, per_try_timeout: 2s` for /v1 endpoints. That could amplify load if backends are overloaded.
maya: hypothesis: backend latency climbed, Envoy retried, causing more concurrent requests -> backend overloaded -> more 5xx. Retry amplification loop.
ops-bot: Running `runbook:lb-retry-loop` -> https://redwood.runbooks/retries
sam: immediate mitigation suggestion: disable retries at gateway for the /v1 route (set num_retries: 0), or reduce to 1 and increase per_try_timeout. Which is faster to roll?
liam: we can hot-reload envoy config via xDS with a small config patch. I'll prepare a minimal patch to set `num_retries: 0` on the offending route.
maya: oncall handoff: I'm pairing with liam, marking this P1. Nisha please help watch customer impact and we should notify success & app teams.
nisha: posting to #customer-impact: "We are investigating elevated 5xx on inference API, potential retry amplification. Working on mitigation. More updates in #incidents"
sam: while config change is prepared, we can reduce LB weight to backend cluster instances to give them breathing room. Recommend 50% traffic to backend_cluster via weight shift to a cached fallback cluster. Thoughts?
liam: I prefer to turn off retries first (lowest risk) then shift weight if errors persist. I'll patch xDS now.
maya: commands I ran to validate current config: ```curl -s http://gateway-01:9901/config_dump | jq '.configs[] | select(.route_config) | .route_config' | grep -A4 "retry_policy"```
liam: patch applied to control plane -> pushing new route config with `num_retries: 0`. Rolling update to envoy via warm restart. Pushing now.
sam: I'm watching metrics: retries count should drop in the next 30s. Also watching backend_latency and inflight connections.
nisha: updating customers (internal status): "Mitigation in progress: disabling gateway retries; next update in 10 minutes."
ops-bot: Deploy event: xDS patch  -> route config change applied to gateway cluster. roll_id=rb-20260315-01
maya: I see retries decreasing: `upstream_rq_retry` dropped from 8k -> 120 in last 2m. Good sign.
liam: 5xx rate trending down from 4.2% -> 1.1% in 4m. Backend p95 latency still elevated but stable.
sam: continuing monitoring. Suggest leaving retries disabled for 30m and consider adding client-side jitter/backoff in SDKs to prevent spikes.
nisha: engaging product ops to assess which customers saw errors. Pulling request logs for error_count by org id. Will follow up with impacted org list.
maya: quick check for circuit breaker pressure: `curl http://gateway-01:9901/stats | grep s_cluster` returned `cluster.backend_cluster.upstream_cx_overflow: 12` and `cluster.backend_cluster.upstream_rq_pending_overflow: 90` earlier. That suggests we pushed queue/pending limits.
liam: lowering cluster max requests and pending limits was attempted in last week's rollout. Might need to revert to previous CB thresholds. Opening rollback PR for circuit breaker changes that reduced pending limits.
sam: action items: 1) keep retries off (liam) 2) revert CB pending limit change (liam) 3) follow-up rate-limiting or weight shift if errors bounce (maya) 4) customer impact list (nisha)
maya: oncall handoff @ 14:45 -> @sam will take primary until 15:30 for watch. I'll update rotation.
ops-bot: Handoff recorded: from maya to sam.
nisha: customer impact snapshot: extracted 43 orgs with >1% error rate, 6 orgs >10% errors. Preparing outbound templates.
sam: logs show a noisy client generating long tail requests, contributing to backend saturation. We should throttle that client if possible. How quickly can product ops block an API key?
maya: product ops can block within ~10m via admin UI. Initiating block for offending API key now.
ops-bot: API key block action taken by maya. key_id=ak-9876 blocked.
liam: after CB rollback and retries off, 5xx stabilized at 0.6%. I'll start the PR to revert the pending limit change with a comment referencing this incident.
maya: postmortem notes to collect: timeline, root cause = retry amplification + aggressive circuit breaker changes, mitigation steps, follow-ups: SDK backoff, rate limit for noisy clients, revert CB change, automated detection rule for retry spikes.
sam: adding to incident board and assigning owners. Also recommend a short customer update after we confirm stability.
nisha: final update to customers (15:30): "Incident mitigated. Retries temporarily disabled at gateway; circuit breaker thresholds reverted. We will follow up with a root cause and timeline." :white_check_mark:
maya: closing watch. Sam, you're primary for the 30m cooldown. If anything spikes, page.
ops-bot: Incident resolved? manual close pending postmortem."
